picks.file: De praecipvis totivs Vniversi vrbibvs, liber secvndvs 1575 (110200297).jpg
picks.what: View across the river, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 2
picks.why: colored profile view of the whole town on the water with the Grote Kerk tower; trimmed to the plate; the center fold shows only as a faint line

picks.file: Van Ruysdael, Salomon, View of Dordrecht, ca. 1660.jpg
picks.what: View across the river, painting (Princeton University Art Museum)
picks.why: the Grote Kerk and town front seen from the water; nearly 16:9 already

picks.file: Johannes Christiaan Schotel - Gezicht op Dordrecht - DM-010-1264 - Dordrechts Museum.jpg
picks.what: View from the river, painting (Dordrechts Museum)
picks.why: Grote Kerk and town across choppy water; museum dates it only to the painter’s working life

picks.what: The Grote Kerk over the Maashaven, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color view of the Grote Kerk tower above the harbor; dark border and caption trimmed

picks.file: NIMH - 2011 - 3587 - Aerial photograph of Dordrecht, The Netherlands.jpg
picks.what: Aerial photograph of the old town and the Grote Kerk (NIMH)
picks.why: the Grote Kerk, harbors and the river front from the air; black negative border trimmed

gaps: P0: nothing; P6: no good modern view
notes: #1–#3 are not medieval: the ‘years’ come from shelf marks (Rembrandt, Lambert Doomer and Jacob van Strij drawings). Braun and Hogenberg vol. 2 view: #4, #6 and #9 are the same plate in bound volumes; #6 chosen for resolution, the fold is a thin line, not a curved gutter. Vol. 3 bird’s-eye plan (#5, #8) passed over for the true view. Van Goyen 1651 (#13) is an equally good, exactly dated P2 alternative; #12 is the same Ruysdael as #11. P3: #15 (1770) and #17 (1803) show the windmills on the Noordendijk but not the town’s landmarks, so Schotel was preferred despite the loose date. #19 is a village near Dordrecht. Modern: #29 is a hazy aerial through clouds, #30 is the Chemours chemical plant across the river, #28 and #31 are gallery photos of 17th-century paintings (Cuyp, van Goyen).
